paper_title: Investigation of Phase Separation in Bulk Heterojunction Solar Cells via Supramolecular Chemistry

knowledge_points.content: The conjugated oligomer NMeTTB is synthesized via Knoevenagel condensation of 5-(2,6-dimethyl-4H-pyran-4-ylidene)-1,3-dimethylpyrimidine-2,4,6(1H,3H,5H)-trione and 3',4'-dihexyl-[2,2':5',2''-terthiophene]-5-carbaldehyde.
knowledge_points.evidence: Knoevenagel condensation of 5-(2,6-dimethyl-4H-pyran-4-ylidene)-1,3-dimethylpyrimidine-2,4,6(1H,3H,5H)-trione with 3',4'-dihexyl-[2,2':5',2''-terthiophene]-5-carbaldehyde gave the targeted derivative... (NMeTTB) as shown in Scheme 1.

knowledge_points.content: The presence of acidic amide protons (N-H) in the barbiturate functional group of TTB facilitates intermolecular hydrogen bonding, leading to the formation of well-ordered nanoribbons, whereas N-methylation in NMeTTB disrupts this self-assembly.
knowledge_points.evidence: TTB has a functional group which undergoes self-assembly by hydrogen bonding, whereas we disrupted the self-assembly by introducing a methyl group in NMeTTB... TTB... showed well-ordered nanoribbons under AFM.

knowledge_points.content: The bulk heterojunction solar cell using NMeTTB:PC61BM (1:1 ratio) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 1.8%, which is significantly higher than the 0.1% PCE achieved by the TTB:PC61BM device.
knowledge_points.evidence: The measured PCE of device A [NMeTTB] is 1.8% which is an order of magnitude higher than that of device B [TTB]... Table 1: Device A PCE 1.8%, Device B PCE 0.1%.

knowledge_points.content: NMeTTB exhibits a hole mobility of approximately 2 x 10^-4 cm^2/(Vs) in organic field-effect transistors (OFETs), which is three orders of magnitude higher than the mobility of TTB (~10^-7 cm^2/(Vs)).
knowledge_points.evidence: The mobility was obtained as ~2 x 10^-4 cm^2/(Vs) for NMeTTB which is higher than mobility of TTB (~10^-7 cm^2/(Vs)) as reported in our earlier paper.

knowledge_points.content: The lower charge carrier mobility in TTB compared to NMeTTB is attributed to the acidic amide protons in the barbiturate group acting as charge carrier traps.
knowledge_points.evidence: We attribute this to the acidic amide proton in TTB which would act as charge carrier traps and results into low mobility.

knowledge_points.content: UV-visible absorption spectra of TTB and NMeTTB show two distinct bands: a higher energy band at 390 nm corresponding to pi-pi* transitions and a lower energy band at 517 nm corresponding to intramolecular charge transfer (ICT).
knowledge_points.evidence: Both derivatives exhibit two absorption bands at 390 and 517 nm in solution. The higher energy band at 390 nm corresponds to π-π* transitions... whereas the low energy band corresponds to intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) of the D-A-D system.

knowledge_points.content: TTB and NMeTTB exhibit solvatochromic behavior where the fluorescence spectra show a bathochromic shift (100 nm for NMeTTB and 60 nm for TTB) in polar solvents due to the stabilization of a zwitterionic D+-A--D excited state.
knowledge_points.evidence: In the case of fluorescence spectra, a bathochromic shift of around 100 nm was observed for NMeTTB and 60 nm for TTB. This was due to the zwitterionic structure D+-A--D... exhibited by D-A-D derivatives in the excited state.

knowledge_points.content: The low open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.34 V in TTB-based devices is likely caused by the chemical reaction of the acidic amide proton with the calcium cathode, forming an insulating layer at the interface.
knowledge_points.evidence: The low Voc in device B may be due to the formation of an insulating layer at the interface between the cathode (calcium) and active layer (TTB). Because, in TTB, the acidic amide proton is very active and may react with calcium...

knowledge_points.content: TTB and NMeTTB both exhibit high thermal stability with decomposition temperatures exceeding 300 °C, and TTB has a higher melting point (209 °C) than NMeTTB (175 °C) due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
knowledge_points.evidence: Both of the compounds are thermally stable with decomposition temperatures of more than 300 °C... DSC indicates phase change at 209 °C for TTB and at 175 °C for NMeTTB... The high melting temperature in the case of TTB is due to intermolecular H-bonding.

knowledge_points.content: DFT calculations show that TTB and NMeTTB possess V-shaped structures with a resultant dipole moment passing through the center of the molecule.
knowledge_points.evidence: Both of these dyes are V-shaped structures which were optimized by DFT calculations (Figure 5). The resultant dipole moment passes through the center of the molecules (TTB and NMeTTB).

knowledge_points.content: Photoluminescence quenching experiments confirm that PC61BM is an effective acceptor for both TTB and NMeTTB, as the donor fluorescence is completely quenched in 1:1 blend films.
knowledge_points.evidence: The photoluminescence of the donor material (oligomer) is completely quenched when blended with PC61BM as an acceptor. This result indicates that PC61BM is a suitable acceptor for TTB and NMeTTB.
